label: Use what is already known
principle: Candidate nomination does not restart the science. Use earlier findings where they apply, and identify what changes with this product, route or clinical setting.

cases.title: Bronchodilation had already been observed in people
cases.stage: Initial US IND review, 2011, reproduced in the 2017 NDA; earlier human studies already existed

steps.label: Before the US IND
steps.text: Two UK single-dose studies had tested glycopyrrolate in people with COPD. The studies included 12 and 42 participants; the larger study reported bronchodilation.

steps.label: The next investigation
steps.text: The US IND proposed a 14-day crossover dose-finding study with a nebulized presentation. The team was moving from earlier single-dose observations to a repeated regimen.

steps.label: What FDA reviewed
steps.text: The initial review used established systemic safety information alongside new inhalation studies addressing local respiratory effects. It considered the proposed trial reasonably safe to proceed.

cases.lesson: Earlier human observations can change the next question. Here, the team already knew the drug could produce bronchodilation in people.
cases.limit: Initial US IND does not mean first human exposure. Single-dose bronchodilation did not establish long-term symptom or exacerbation benefit, or suitability of every inhaled presentation.

sources.label: Proposed study and prior UK experience · PDF 38–39

cases.title: Related-enzyme studies did not answer every product question
cases.stage: 2014 preliminary IND review excerpt reproduced in the 2017 BLA; not all studies are established as preceding first human exposure

steps.label: Earlier enzyme experiments
steps.text: Published mouse studies used recombinant murine enzyme. Tissue correction differed between repeated treatment from birth and a later single injection; not every tissue improved.

steps.label: The human product
steps.text: The review separately summarized uptake of recombinant human enzyme into cells from people with MPS VII. That addressed whether the product could enter relevant cells.

steps.label: Activity after uptake
steps.text: A separate product study compared two lots by following intracellular enzyme activity after removing enzyme from the medium. It examined persistence of activity, not just initial uptake.

cases.lesson: Keep related-product evidence, but ask what the actual candidate must still demonstrate: entry into cells, continued function and access to affected tissues.
cases.limit: The uptake study report was not submitted. Intracellular persistence is not plasma half-life, and murine-enzyme experiments do not establish human brain benefit or a human dosing interval.

sources.label: Product studies and published mouse experiments · PDF 16–20

label: Show what this drug actually does
principle: Binding a target, changing a cell and changing a disease model are different findings. Describe what the experiment showed before claiming what the drug will do in people.

cases.title: The second target was tested against an anti-VEGF comparator
cases.stage: Studies explicitly attributed to the initial IND, summarized in the 2022 BLA; corrected study data are identified

steps.label: Two binding activities
steps.text: Binding experiments showed that faricimab could bind VEGF-A and ANG-2 independently and simultaneously. This established two interactions, but did not show what the second interaction added.

steps.label: A functional comparison
steps.text: A study of laser-induced abnormal blood vessels in the choroid used three monkeys per group. Faricimab was compared with ranibizumab, an anti-ANG-2 antibody and an antibody control.

steps.label: What changed
steps.text: At matched anti-VEGF binding sites, 90 micrograms of faricimab reduced lesion severity more than 30 micrograms of ranibizumab in this experiment.

cases.lesson: A functional comparison can test whether a proposed additional action changes an outcome beyond what the existing action achieves.
cases.limit: A small induced-lesion model does not establish better vision in people, clinical superiority or pharmacological synergy. The review identifies corrected data without supplying the full correction history.

cases.title: Receptor occupancy did not establish D2 partial agonism
cases.stage: NDA account of the 2007 initial IND and 2014 meeting, followed by a separate NDA mechanism assessment

steps.label: Initial human question
steps.text: The initial IND proposed an open-label receptor-occupancy study. FDA allowed it to proceed in November 2007: the study could examine engagement of receptors in people.

steps.label: Later dose planning
steps.text: In 2014, FDA suggested considering receptor occupancy together with dose-response information when choosing Phase 3 doses.

steps.label: The broader claim
steps.text: At NDA review, FDA questioned the claim of presynaptic D2 partial agonism. In-vitro tests showed D2 antagonism; the reviewer found the evidence insufficient for the proposed presynaptic action.

cases.lesson: Measuring receptor engagement is different from identifying what the drug does at that receptor or how patients benefit.
cases.limit: The initial IND history is retrospective. The later mechanistic criticism and labeling decision must not be presented as findings made before the 2007 study.

sources.label: Initial IND and later meeting history · PDF 34

moreCases.finding: JAK1/JAK2 selectivity seen in isolated-enzyme experiments was not reproduced in human-leukocyte assays. The reviewer also noted that exposure estimates for a rat efficacy experiment came from a separate experiment.
moreCases.lesson: An enzyme-assay label may not describe intact-cell behavior. State where exposure and response were actually measured together.
moreCases.stage: 2018 NDA pharmacology assessment; these studies are not established as the original IND set
moreCases.limit: Cell assays do not settle clinical selectivity in every tissue, and separate-animal exposure estimates are not paired exposure-response observations.

sources.label: Rat efficacy and exposure limitation · PDF 84–86

moreCases.finding: FDA requested fungal-growth information from untreated control mice to judge whether the models and strains were suitable for interpreting drug activity and PK/PD targets.
moreCases.lesson: To interpret a treated group, first understand what happened without treatment.
moreCases.stage: March 2022 preliminary pre-NDA comments under an IND; not final meeting agreements or initial-IND advice
moreCases.limit: A request for control data does not prove that the sponsor never collected those data.

moreCases.finding: The review describes activity in models driven by FLT3 or JAK2 mutations and links kinase inhibition with reduced activated STAT proteins. Its history records two initial Phase 1 malignancy protocols considered safe to proceed in February 2008.
moreCases.lesson: Kinase inhibition, pathway changes and tumor-model activity each contribute a different observation to the rationale.
moreCases.stage: 2022 NDA account of initial IND history plus IND-submitted pharmacology summaries; individual study submission dates are not all specified
moreCases.limit: Later clinical-exposure analyses in the review were not knowledge available before first dosing; model activity did not establish the eventual best population.

sources.label: Initial history and IND pharmacology · PDF 101–103

moreCases.finding: FDA noted a concentration mismatch: proposed neuroprotection at low-to-mid nanomolar concentrations, but glutamate-receptor binding at micromolar concentrations. Separate functional NMDA-receptor experiments showed no significant agonism or antagonism up to 30 micromolar.
moreCases.lesson: A mechanism must make sense at the concentrations where the relevant effect occurs.
moreCases.stage: 2023 NDA controlled-substance consultation recounting later IND assessment and reviewing additional NDA functional data
moreCases.limit: This consultation examines particular mechanistic claims; it does not establish the complete rationale for benefit in Rett syndrome.

sources.label: Concentration mismatch and functional assays · PDF 22–23

label: Explain why that could help
principle: Connect the observed drug action to the problem being treated. The drug may work around a defect, and a useful treatment can still have an incomplete explanation of benefit.

cases.title: Blocking an earlier step could reduce harmful products
cases.stage: NDA assessment in the 2002 approval package; its pathway figure is explicitly drawn from a January 1995 IND review

steps.label: The disease defect
steps.text: Hereditary tyrosinemia type 1 involves a deficient enzyme late in tyrosine breakdown. Harmful metabolites accumulate along that pathway.

steps.label: The drug’s action
steps.text: Nitisinone inhibits an enzyme earlier in the pathway. The intervention reduces production of harmful downstream substances rather than replacing the deficient enzyme.

steps.label: Another consequence
steps.text: The review describes reduced urinary succinylacetone during treatment, but also increased tyrosine and ocular injury in rat studies. Blocking a pathway can create a different metabolic problem.

cases.lesson: A drug can help without repairing the original defect. Explain both the useful change and the other consequences of changing the pathway.
cases.limit: Only the pathway figure is explicitly attributed to the 1995 IND here. The surrounding animal and clinical summaries come from the later NDA assessment.

sources.label: Disease pathway and drug action · PDF 9–10

cases.title: The replacement hypothesis did not explain everything
cases.stage: NDA account of the 2014 postpartum-depression IND, followed by later pharmacology and benefit-risk assessments

steps.label: The starting hypothesis
steps.text: Allopregnanolone falls after childbirth. A replacement hypothesis helped focus brexanolone development on postpartum depression; the drug is chemically identical to allopregnanolone and modulates GABA-A receptors.

steps.label: The proposed test
steps.text: The June 2014 indication-specific IND proposed an open-label Phase 2a study in adult women with severe postpartum depression. FDA found the protocol safe to proceed.

steps.label: The later assessment
steps.text: The NDA review notes that allopregnanolone levels did not predict postpartum depression and that the mechanism of benefit remained unknown. Controlled trials supplied clinical evidence beyond the replacement hypothesis.

cases.lesson: A hypothesis can guide a useful clinical investigation without becoming a complete explanation of the disease or the treatment’s benefit.
cases.limit: The initial postpartum-depression IND was not necessarily first human exposure. The review does not date when the replacement explanation weakened; later findings must not be backdated to that IND.

moreCases.finding: A 2017 IND review reported no pharmacology studies with the foam and an unknown acne mechanism. Later formulation testing showed antibacterial activity, while pivotal trials measured acne lesions and investigator-rated severity rather than clinical microbiology outcomes.
moreCases.lesson: Knowing an antibacterial action is different from proving how that action accounts for improvement in acne.
moreCases.stage: 2017 later IND review reproduced in the 2019 NDA; separate later microbiology and clinical assessments
moreCases.modality: Small molecule · Topical formulation of an established drug
moreCases.limit: The statement about absent foam pharmacology concerns that retained review. It is not a general exemption for novel candidates or all later studies.

moreCases.finding: The sponsor emphasized Nrf2 signaling, but the NDA review described several possible pathways. Nrf2 contributed to one macrophage effect without being required for it, and gene responses differed across tissues.
moreCases.lesson: Evidence that a pathway participates does not establish that it is the only explanation, or that it is necessary for every effect.
moreCases.stage: 2013 NDA primary-pharmacology assessment; these findings are not established as the initial IND evidence
moreCases.limit: The passage does not establish FDA acceptance of Nrf2 as the initial IND efficacy mechanism or a predictive patient-selection marker.

sources.label: Multiple pathways and model findings · PDF 41–42

moreCases.finding: Parkinson disease psychosis posed a practical problem: some antipsychotics worsened movement. Selective serotonergic pharmacology offered a different approach, but the clinical reviewer still described the disease mechanism and explanation of benefit as uncertain.
moreCases.lesson: A drug can address a specific clinical problem without explaining the whole disease. Animal effects do not establish that clinical advantage.
moreCases.stage: 2016 NDA clinical and pharmacology assessments; not established as the original IND package
moreCases.limit: These are reviewer assessments, not proof that the proposed motor advantage follows from receptor selectivity alone.

sources.label: Clinical problem and uncertain mechanism · PDF 21–22, 27

moreCases.finding: The original-IND appendix combines receptor profiling with ovulation-inhibition and other functional experiments. It tests a physiological intervention for contraception rather than repair of a disease-causing defect.
moreCases.lesson: Connect pharmacology to the intended useful function; potential benefit need not mean correcting a disease mechanism.
moreCases.stage: Original IND appendix reproduced in the 2001 NDA pharmacology review
moreCases.limit: Receptor activity and animal ovulation inhibition do not, by themselves, establish clinical contraceptive effectiveness.

sources.label: Original-IND receptor and functional studies · PDF 38–40

moreCases.finding: Bupropion increases dextromethorphan exposure by inhibiting its metabolism. At the 2019 end-of-Phase-2 meeting, FDA agreed that dextromethorphan alone at the combination dose would be metabolized too rapidly for the proposed direct comparison; component-contribution evidence still mattered.
moreCases.lesson: When drugs are combined, ask what each adds at the exposure the combination actually produces.
moreCases.stage: NDA account of later IND/end-of-Phase-2 advice in 2019, plus NDA pharmacology assessment
moreCases.limit: Conditional study-design advice was not a promise of approval. The exact antidepressant mechanism remained unknown.
